summary: The candidate fixes the reproduced nonzero-reserved-slot prompt accounting case and passes its regression suite, but still silently accepts an impossible request when configured EAGLE reserved slots exceed the model context. Its HTTP/GPU smoke has speculative decoding disabled and therefore does not exercise the changed path.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before on the exact recorded base: reserved-token prompt truncation retained 10 prompt tokens instead of the context-safe 7; the other three candidate tests passed.
Exact candidate source checkout: 11 tests and 11 subtests passed, including the reproduced reserved-slot regression and adjacent validation compatibility.

Independent boundaries. Normal prompt/completion and reserved=3 cases fit context after truncation; disabled mode raises. Counterexample: context=10 and reserved=11 returns without error with accounted total=11.

gpu_execution.evidence: No independent GPU execution was needed for Python request-budget arithmetic. The candidate's retained MI355X/gfx950 HTTP evidence was inspected, but speculative_algorithm=None means it did not exercise the changed reserved-token path.

remaining_counterexamples: With context_len=10 and num_reserved_tokens=11, auto-truncation returns normally after reducing prompt and completion to zero even though the accounted total remains 11 > 10.
remaining_limitations: No qualified EAGLE draft model was available, so nonzero reserved-token behavior was validated directly at TokenizerManager rather than end-to-end on GPU.
The deterministic tiny-Llama HTTP fixture can validate transport and engine execution only and cannot validate the EAGLE-specific changed path without a compatible speculative draft model.
No native source changed; native rebuild and compiler/ISA validation were not applicable.
Independent GPU numerical comparison is not applicable to this request-validation control flow.
